angle: Free virtual staging almost always means a watermarked preview you cannot put on a listing. This post says what free actually includes, and proves it by making the image on the free tier's own model rather than the paid one.
visualSummary: Two stacked panels on the deep blue field. The top panel is muted red and carries the belief that free means a watermarked preview, with a short concession under it. The bottom panel is brand blue and states that free means the finished file, with a note naming what is included and what is not. Sitting inside the right edge of the blue panel, faded in from the left, is a warm crop of a midcentury kitchen render: a cream retro range with chrome trim and six knobs, a cream fridge, patterned cream and gold tile, amber oak cabinets and a sliver of fruit bowl on the counter.

copy.headline: Free is not a teaser.
copy.caption:
Free virtual staging usually means a watermarked preview. Ours means the file you put on the listing.

The kitchen in this post was rendered on the free tier. Not a screenshot from the paid plan, not a demo account. The free one.

What free includes:

All eight room types. Bedroom, living room, dining room, kitchen, office, bathroom, outdoors and dorm.
All seven style presets.
The full size file, with no watermark on it.
No card to start.

What it does not:

Stagify+ is $11.99 a month. It adds furniture removal, the masking tool, the AI Designer, several variations per render, and a higher quality image model. That last one matters here, because this post was made on the free model. What you are looking at is the floor, not the ceiling.

Most tools show you the good version and charge you before you find out which one you were shown. Upload a room and see the free one first.

generation.modelNote: DELIBERATE SINGLE-POST DEPARTURE FROM RULE 3, and the reason the post works. Rule 3 pins gemini-3.1-flash-image because the image is the product demo and a weak render is worse than no post. But getGeminiImageModel (lib/config/model-config.js) maps a free account to gemini-2.5-flash-image and a Stagify+ account to gemini-3.1-flash-image, so 3.1 is the PAID tier's output. A post whose entire claim is what the free tier gives you cannot show a paid render and call it free. Rule 3 forbids economising on a demo; it does not license overstating the free tier. Everything else about rule 3 was kept: full retry loop, never skipQualityReview, three attempts per photo and two different source photos. acquire.js gained one additive passthrough (brief.model), undefined everywhere else, so no other post changes behaviour.
generation.authorNote: Rule 4 applied: quality.perfect was false, so the render was opened at full size before anything was written. The automated reviewer flagged stool legs on five of six attempts, and at full zoom that flag is wrong: both stools have four complete legs with correct splay, a ring footrest and feet meeting the floor with visible contact shadows. The real defect is one it mentioned once, the glass vessel right of the coffee maker, which is doubled, semi-transparent and has no base. A revision round (posts/_work/restage-0816.mjs) re-staged the same source with the counters cleared. It removed that artifact and introduced a worse one: the three pendant globes bunched into an overlapping clump at the top right, plus a stool cut by the frame edge and two illegible sticker-like marks on the backsplash. That render was discarded and this one kept, with the crop doing the work instead.

review.authorRounds: Two author revisions BEFORE the reviewer saw it, both from opening the render rather than reading a score. Round A: the first render put a doubled, semi-transparent glass vessel on the counter, so the same source was re-staged with the counters cleared; that fixed the vessel and bunched the three pendant globes into an overlapping clump at the top right, which is worse, so it was discarded and the crop used instead. Round B: the first composite orphaned the word 'photo.' onto its own headline line and left the myth panel two thirds empty against a dense fact panel, so the headline was cut to a single line and the myth line and note were lengthened to balance the two cards.
nits: A thin chrome rail leaves the range backguard, runs diagonally down and right past the range's rear corner and terminates in mid air over the gap to the fridge, attached to nothing. Inside the published crop, and the reviewer's pick for the most AI-looking element in the frame. Kept: it reads as an ordinary backguard handrail at feed size and only fails on inspection, and the alternative render failed worse and more visibly.
The six range knobs each carry a tiny index mark that is pseudo-lettering rather than a real glyph or tick. 2 to 3px at delivery size.
The fridge door badge is an illegible brand-mark scribble, bisected by the right edge of the photo panel. About a 6px smudge at delivery size.
The glass fruit bowl's right rim melts into the range's stainless corner trim. Almost entirely under the gradient in the published composite.

The fact panel's body copy measures 4.05:1 against the brand blue card. That clears AA for large text and misses the 4.5:1 normal-text threshold; every other run in the frame is 6.0:1 or better. This is .panel__note's rgba(255,255,255,.78) in templates/myth-fact/template.css, so it is the TEMPLATE's number, not this post's. Left alone deliberately: raising it here means restyling shared chrome for one post, which is rule 13 backwards. Worth fixing in the template before myth-fact runs again.
The visible sliver of photograph after the gradient is fridge, backsplash and half a range, so the copy says 'this kitchen' and the reader sees a corner of one.
review.dashAudit: Zero dash-family characters anywhere in the frame, hyphens included, across all eleven text runs. Checked glyph by glyph at 2160px master resolution rather than asserted. The two near-misses were measured and cleared: the colon in 'means:' is two stacked dots with no horizontal stroke and its ink height matches the adjacent 'n' x-height, and every sentence terminator is a round period about 0.25 of an 'n' wide. The only long horizontal stroke in the frame is the fake brand mark on the fridge door inside the photograph, roughly 3n wide, well above any text baseline and not a character. No line in either paragraph breaks on a hyphen.
review.contrast: 6.03:1 to 7.53:1 on every run except the fact note at 4.05:1. No type sits over the photograph anywhere: the fact copy ends around x730 of 1600 and the photo starts near x1000, with the gradient covering the band between, so rule 10 is satisfied by construction rather than by a scrim. The disclosure line is present, unobscured and at full opacity.
review.samenessVerdict: Not a rerun, and the reviewer named the real risk rather than clearing it: against 08-15 this shares the deep blue ground, the top-left lockup, the small-caps kicker top-right, a white headline with a pale blue clause, a photo block low in the frame and the disclosure plus white CTA pill in the footer. That is two consecutive deep-blue type-led posts on the same skeleton. What separates them is a giant numeral over a full-width band versus a stacked two-card argument with the photo bleeding into the right half of the lower card. Nothing like 08-14, 08-13 or the two legacy split-screens. Composition is distinct, colour is not. The blue-ground streak is a watch item for 08-17, not a defect here.

devilsAdvocate.whyThisOne: Chosen by the user over the advocate's pick, and over the advocate having KILLED it outright. The advocate's kill was that the post either prints the real free cap of 50 a day, landing the reader on a homepage that says 'Free, as often as you like', or drops the number and becomes a myth-fact card with no fact. The first horn is real and was confirmed in source: public/index.html carries an explicit comment that naming the cap reads as a smaller offer, and test/frontend/pricing-copy.test.js pins the ABSENCE of a figure in that key across all eleven language packs. So the number is out. The second horn is what the build answered: the fact is not a number, it is the image. Rendering on gemini-2.5-flash-image makes the post's own proof the thing it is claiming.
devilsAdvocate.residualRisk: The post argues honesty and then spends a paragraph of caption on what free does NOT include, including the admission that the reader is looking at the weaker model. That is the point, but it is also a conversion tax: a reader who wanted to be impressed is told, on the frame that is meant to sell them, that a better version exists behind $11.99. If it underperforms, the diagnosis is almost certainly that paragraph, and the fix is not to delete it but to move it later in the caption, below the fold at 125 characters.
